newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong handover to take stocks to dizzy highs.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong handover to take stocks to dizzy highs.

text.p: The excitement of Hong Kong's handover to Chinese rule will intoxicate the stock market, taking the Hang Seng to new dizzying highs in the next two years, a Reuters survey of the outlook for the world's top bourses found.
There was no disagreement about the Hang Seng's direction among six equity specialists who took part in the survey. The question was simply how high it would go.
On average their predictions amounted to a 16 percent gain to around 15,270 points from Wednesday's levels in Hong Kong of around 13,150. The lowest forecasts, too, were above current prices.
Two suggested the index would finish 1997 above 16,000.

In 1998, for which five forecasts were contributed, the mean forecast held out the prospect of further heady heights. One predicted the market would not settle until it had touched 20,000 over the next two years.
Following is a selection of quotes from analysts who contributed Hang Seng forecasts to the survey:
KENT ROSSITER, INSTITUTIONAL SALES MANAGER AT NIKKO SECURITIES
"Sometime between 1997 and 98 it will go above 20,000...The euphoria is likely to settle in the year, year and a half following the handover."
"People are talking about a PE re-rating and it has not happened yet. PE valuations are not unduly expensive."
ALEX TANG, HEAD OF RESEARCH AT YAMAICHI INTERNATIONAL
"The China factor has been turning more positive and mainland funds are coming to Hong Kong buying property and equities. There are signs that more will be coming."
